title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
headline: Instead of writing one answer left to right, a language model lays out partial answers as a branching tree, scores each branch itself, and searches the tree, keeping the promising paths and backtracking out of dead ends.
abstract: Language models are increasingly being deployed for general problem solving across a wide range of tasks, but are still confined to token-level, left-to-right decision-making processes during inference. This means they can fall short in tasks that require exploration, strategic lookahead, or where initial decisions play a pivotal role. To surmount these challenges, we introduce a new framework for language model inference, "Tree of Thoughts" (ToT), which generalizes over the popular "Chain of Thought" approach to prompting language models, and enables exploration over coherent units of text ("thoughts") that serve as intermediate steps toward problem solving. ToT allows LMs to perform deliberate decision making by considering multiple different reasoning paths and self-evaluating choices to decide the next course of action, as well as looking ahead or backtracking when necessary to make global choices. Our experiments show that ToT significantly enhances language models' problem-solving abilities on three novel tasks requiring non-trivial planning or search: Game of 24, Creative Writing, and Mini Crosswords. For instance, in Game of 24, while GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting only solved 4% of tasks, our method achieved a success rate of 74%.

images.alt: A pixel-art field-journal map where a single trailhead splits into a branching tree of forest trails, a few lit clay-orange trails traced by ink arrows climbing to a glowing lantern marked goal while the other trails fade to gray and dead-end with x marks, showing that Tree of Thoughts explores many partial-answer branches, keeps the promising ones, and searches its way to the answer.
images.caption: One start, many branching trails. The search keeps the promising routes lit and lets the dead ends fade.

images.alt: A forest trail splitting into three forks at a junction with an ink wax-seal stamp on each path reading sure, maybe, and no, and a small ink magnifier at the junction, showing that the language model both proposes the next steps and grades each one before the search decides which to follow.
images.caption: The model plays two roles at every fork. It proposes the next steps, then grades each one sure, maybe, or no.

images.alt: A forest trail that climbs into a pile of boulders blocking the way, with a bold curved ink arrow labelled backtrack looping back down to the last fork where a fresh clay-orange trail sets off in a new direction, showing that depth-first search prunes a dead-end branch and backs up to try another.
images.caption: Hit a dead end, cut that branch, and back up to the last fork to try a different route.

images.alt: Two small trail maps side by side, on the left a single narrow trail labelled b=1 that dead-ends short of the top, on the right a wide fan of several trails labelled b=5 where one clay-orange trail reaches a glowing lantern, showing that keeping more branches alive at each step finds the goal far more often.
images.caption: Keep one branch and a single bad score loses the answer. Keep five and the winning route survives.
